results.name: inside_range_by_setsize_slope
results.description: Slope, across number of examples (2-4), of the yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' min-max range; observed above null_mean means people fill in the spanned range increasingly with more examples than the model predicts, below means the model's size-principle tightening is too weak/strong in the opposite way.
results.code:
# name: inside_range_by_setsize_slope
# description: Slope, across number of examples (2-4), of the yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' min-max range; observed above null_mean means people fill in the spanned range increasingly with more examples than the model predicts, below means the model's size-principle tightening is too weak/strong in the opposite way.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    notex = ~np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    m = (n_ex >= 2) & notex & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    xs, ys = [], []
    for k in (2, 3, 4):
        s = m & (n_ex == k)
        if s.any():
            xs.append(k)
            ys.append(r[s].mean())
    if len(xs) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.polyfit(np.array(xs, float), np.array(ys), 1)[0])

results.name: near_vs_mid_distance_gap
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets 1-5 from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 6-20 away; observed above null_mean means people show a steeper local similarity gradient than the model's interval/rule mixture (model's generalisation too flat or non-monotone near examples).
results.code:
# name: near_vs_mid_distance_gap
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets 1-5 from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 6-20 away; observed above null_mean means people show a steeper local similarity gradient than the model's interval/rule mixture (model's generalisation too flat or non-monotone near examples).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    a = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 5)
    b = (dist >= 6) & (dist <= 20)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: far_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets more than 40 away from every example; observed above null_mean means people say yes to remote numbers more than the model's rules/intervals allow (missing lapse/guessing floor), below means the model over-generalises far away.
results.code:

# description: Yes rate for targets more than 40 away from every example; observed above null_mean means people say yes to remote numbers more than the model's rules/intervals allow (missing lapse/guessing floor), below means the model over-generalises far away.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = dist > 40
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: target_is_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials whose target equals one of the shown examples; observed below null_mean means the model is too confident that examples belong to the concept (people need a lapse/noise floor at the top).
results.code:
# name: target_is_example_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate on trials whose target equals one of the shown examples; observed below null_mean means the model is too confident that examples belong to the concept (people need a lapse/noise floor at the top).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    m = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: parity_consistency_gap
results.description: Among sets with >=2 examples all of one parity, yes rate for non-example targets of the same parity minus targets of the opposite parity; observed above null_mean means people use parity more than the model (which under-weights odd/even rules), below means the model over-uses parity.
results.code:
# name: parity_consistency_gap
# description: Among sets with >=2 examples all of one parity, yes rate for non-example targets of the same parity minus targets of the opposite parity; observed above null_mean means people use parity more than the model (which under-weights odd/even rules), below means the model over-uses parity.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    par = np.mod(E, 2)
    p0 = par[:, 0]
    same = np.all((par == p0[:, None]) | np.isnan(par), axis=1) & (n_ex >= 2)
    notex = ~np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    tp = np.mod(t, 2) == p0
    a = same & notex & tp
    b = same & notex & ~tp
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: shared_last_digit_far_yes_rate
results.description: Among sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for targets with that same last digit lying >15 from every example; observed below null_mean means the model still over-extends "ends in d" guesses to distant numbers, above means it under-weights digit rules.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_far_yes_rate
# description: Among sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for targets with that same last digit lying >15 from every example; observed below null_mean means the model still over-extends "ends in d" guesses to distant numbers, above means it under-weights digit rules.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    ld = np.mod(E, 10)
    first = ld[:, 0]
    same = np.all((ld == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(ld), axis=1) & (n_ex >= 2)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = same & (np.mod(t, 10) == first) & (dist > 15)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: first_vs_last_example_proximity_gap
results.description: For multi-example sets, yes rate on non-example targets within 10 of the first example (and >10 from the last) minus those within 10 of the last example (and >10 from the first); observed below null_mean means people weight later examples more (recency) than the model's first-example sticky guess predicts, above means stronger primacy.
results.code:
# name: first_vs_last_example_proximity_gap
# description: For multi-example sets, yes rate on non-example targets within 10 of the first example (and >10 from the last) minus those within 10 of the last example (and >10 from the first); observed below null_mean means people weight later examples more (recency) than the model's first-example sticky guess predicts, above means stronger primacy.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    last = E[np.arange(len(E)), np.maximum(n_ex - 1, 0)]
    d1 = np.abs(E[:, 0] - t)
    dl = np.abs(last - t)
    notex = ~np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    multi = n_ex >= 2
    a = multi & notex & (d1 <= 10) & (dl > 10)
    b = multi & notex & (dl <= 10) & (d1 > 10)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: trial_index_yes_slope
results.description: OLS slope of yes (0/1) on trial_index scaled per 100 trials; observed more negative than null_mean means people grow more conservative over the session, a drift the stationary model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: trial_index_yes_slope
# description: OLS slope of yes (0/1) on trial_index scaled per 100 trials; observed more negative than null_mean means people grow more conservative over the session, a drift the stationary model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["trial_index"].astype(float).values / 100.0
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    vx = np.var(x)
    return float(np.cov(x, y, bias=True)[0, 1] / vx) if vx > 0 else 0.0
